scope: Synthetic local POSIX filesystem experiment only; no model or network; not MCP protocol conformance.
guarantees_tested: path traversal and symlink rejection including final-component symlink substitution
principal/path/content binding and mutable argument snapshot
atomic no-clobber publication under 2 competing approvals
temporary file cleanup on controlled I/O failures
limitations: The host, approval issuer, principal mapping and process memory are trusted. Do not expose approve_store or approval tokens as model tools/data.

Root trees must be service-owned without untrusted OS writers. This does not sandbox a hostile local user, privileged attacker, hard links, bind mounts or concurrent directory moves outside an opened root.
Approvals are held in memory, have no expiration/durable audit and are lost on restart; I/O failure consumes the token.
Atomic publication uses local POSIX hard-link no-clobber semantics; Windows and network/distributed filesystems are not validated.
No power-loss/crash persistence, HTTP authentication, real MCP server/client, prompt-injection benchmark or production security certification.
